title: Do not diagnose an Amazon Store conversion drop from mixed attribution variants
scenario: A Sponsored Brands campaign serving in the Amazon Store appears to lose ROAS immediately after January 1, 2026. The pre-cutover baseline was retained from a view-attributed reporting path that effectively represented all eligible ad views over a 14-day window, while the post-cutover analyst uses the new standard Purchases, Sales and ROAS fields under Amazon's shopping-signal enhanced last-touch methodology. Spend and click-side traffic are broadly stable. The analyst wants to cut bids and add negatives because the conversion KPI appears to have fallen.

inputs.observed_claim: ROAS fell about 23%, so cut bids and add negatives immediately.

forbidden_behaviors: Treat baseline and comparison Purchases, Sales or ROAS as definitionally continuous merely because they belong to the same conversion metric family.
Attribute the apparent ROAS drop to bid, targeting, search-term quality or retail performance before reconciling the attribution variants.
Cut bids, add negatives, pause traffic or roll back another optimization solely from the unreconciled conversion decline.
Substitute all-views metrics for standard metrics, or standard metrics for all-views metrics, without labeling the attribution definition change.
Assume every Amazon Ads campaign type and inventory type experienced the same January 2026 view-attribution change.
required_observations: The January 1, 2026 Amazon Store ads update made a shopping-signal enhanced last-touch methodology standard for specified eligible view-attributed inventory while retaining separate all-views conversion metrics for eligible campaigns.
Attribution variant is part of metric identity; standard Purchases/Sales/ROAS and all-views Purchases/Sales/ROAS are not automatically comparable despite sharing a metric family.

The apparent break coincides with a measurement-methodology cutover and must remain a competing measurement cause until the two windows are replayed under one compatible attribution variant or reconciled through an overlap/bridge.

Stable click-side evidence can be supporting context because Amazon documented click-based attribution as unchanged for this specific update, but it does not by itself prove conversion performance was unchanged.

rubric.requirement: Represent attribution_variant explicitly and identify the January 2026 methodology boundary.
Do not mix standard and all-views conversion variants as one continuous Purchases/Sales/ROAS series.
Treat the methodology cutover as a competing cause before diagnosing advertising deterioration.
Apply the documented attribution change only to eligible campaign/inventory scope rather than generalizing to all Amazon Ads traffic.
Block bid cuts, negatives, pauses, rollback or scaling decisions from the unreconciled apparent ROAS delta.
